title: Inheritance record
description: Stage 3. Same corpus, different question: where does the author engage a predecessor, and in what mode. The mode column is what turns a citation list into a genealogy, so it is required and closed.

model.description: Model identifier for the pass, as the provider names it (e.g. claude-opus-5). Optional, and never supplied from memory: a record written before this field existed omits it rather than guessing which model wrote it.

predecessors_queried.description: The names this pass used as retrieval keys, as searched ('Heidegger', 'neo-Kantian'). A name listed here with no engagement means searched and nothing found that does work in one of the five modes; a name absent from it means not searched. Omit it when the whole commentary was read (coverage complete), and never reconstruct it for an older pass whose note does not say what was searched.

text.description: The predecessor text, only where the commentary identifies it. Omit rather than infer.

locator.description: Where in the predecessor's text the engagement bears, as the commentary cites it ('Ideas I § 42', 'A 141 / B 180', '§§ 62-74'). It names a P-locus for a comparative run, so only a citation the commentary itself gives; never supplied, never converted to another edition.

mode.description: The last value is a local addition: Destruktion takes over a concept and dismantles its received sense in one move, which neither rejection nor borrowing describes. Use it only where the commentary presents both halves.
